# `silk/mem/interned`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Handles to values that never change and are never freed, so a handle is a plain pointer.

## When to use
Use [`Interned`](#Interned) for values that live as long as the program phase that makes them, such as the
hash-consed types of one compiler check. Copying a handle touches no memory, and a value can be
read from any thread once its handle is published.

## Gotchas
The value is never dropped. Use `silk.mem.frozen.Frozen` for a value that should be freed.

## Examples
### Copy a handle and read through both
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.interned { Interned }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let first = run Interned<i32>.make(40) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let second = Interned<i32>.clone(&first)
  let sum = Interned<i32>.get(&first).* + Interned<i32>.get(&second).*
  if sum != 80 || !Interned<i32>.same(&first, &second) { return 1 }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Interned` with `import silk.mem.interned { Interned }`.

Public declarations: 1.

## `Interned`

```silk
pub struct Interned<T>
```

A handle to one value of type `T` that never changes and is never freed.

<a id="Interned.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Interned<T>`

```silk
impl<T> Interned<T>
```

<a id="Interned.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn make<'env>(value: T) -> Interned<T> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Allocates storage that is never freed and moves `value` into it.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. `value` is dropped.

<a id="Interned.impl.discard"></a>

### Associated function `discard`

```silk
pub unsafe fn discard(handle: Interned<T>) -> ()
```

Frees a value that no other handle refers to, such as one made only to look up an equal value
that already has a handle.

#### Safety

`handle` is the only handle to its value: it was never cloned.

<a id="Interned.impl.clone"></a>

### Method `clone`

```silk
pub fn clone(self: &Self) -> Interned<T>
```

Returns another handle to the same value. It copies one pointer.

<a id="Interned.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get<'a>(self: &'a Self) -> &'a T
```

Borrows the value for as long as this handle is borrowed.

<a id="Interned.impl.with"></a>

### Method `with`

```silk
pub fn with<A>(self: &Self, use: once fn(&T) -> A) -> A
```

Calls `use` one time with a shared borrow of the value and returns the result of `use`.


The address of the value, which every handle to it shares.
